title: A triangle whose two morph targets are driven by an animated weight pair -- four frames of its declared 4 s span

criterion.says: A triangle with a morph animation applied

acceptanceClass.because: The framing rule's own direction over a subject whose VERTICES move rather than whose node does. The animated path is `weights`, so nothing about the node transform changes and the axis convention that every other animated case has to derive does not enter: what is compared is where the displaced vertices land at each sampled time.

blender.note: A release version, not a commit. Recorded so a red rung can be attributed to our renderer or to the oracle, and carried in the oracle's cache key so a version bump misses instead of serving a stale render. We do not aim to be bit-identical with Cycles.

subjects.name: SimpleMorph
subjects.notes: Attributes POSITION, COLOR_0 with two morph targets. 1 animation over a declared span of 4 s targeting node 0, which is the mesh node itself and therefore an ORDINARY OBJECT in Blender -- not a joint. That is why this one is authorable where the skinned cases of board:1375 are not.

source.pinReason: the corpus-wide pin every manifest in this tree already cites

camera.derivation: The framing rule of src/gltf/Framing.h, quoted so the runner can refuse a mismatch rather than trust it. World bounds [0.0, 0.0, 0.0] to [1.0, 0.5, 0.0], so centre = [0.5, 0.25, 0.0] and radius = 0.5590169943749475 m. yfov = 2*atan(12/50) from a 50 mm lens on a 24 mm sensor height at sensor_fit VERTICAL. distance = radius / sin(yfov/2) / 0.6 = 3.9923006532791145, and the eye is centre + (cos20*cos35, sin20, cos20*sin35) * distance. clipStart is distance - radius and clipEnd is distance + radius.
camera.note: THE ENGINE'S OWN ANSWER, QUOTED (board:1398). Every number here is read from the framing rule's output for this subject -- eye, aim, yfov and both clip planes -- rather than recomputed by the authoring helper, which bounded each primitive by the eight transformed corners of its local AABB and therefore always at least as loosely as the engine bounds the transformed vertices. A looser radius moves the eye back, and 93 cases declared a camera the rule does not derive. `ADerivedCameraIsTheFramingRuleAndNotAQuotation` recomputes all of it and refuses a mismatch, so what this declaration does is PIN the viewpoint, never choose it.

light.note: The material emits, so nothing has to arrive for the picture to exist.

world.note: Declared and zero rather than left factory, so the picture is a function of this manifest and not of a Blender default.

material.note: Emission, one colour per glTF material, keyed by the name the FILE gives it. A material a primitive does not name is keyed by `<default>`, which is the format's own word for the material an undefined `material` selects.

fps.note: ONE FRAME PER SECOND, AND THE RATE IS AN INTEGER BECAUSE THE HARNESS REQUIRES ONE: a frame is `index / fps` seconds and Blender's own rate is whole.

frames.derivation: min(5, ceil(4.0 s) + 1) = 5, so the grid runs 0..4 s.
frames.note: The file's declared span is 4 s and this grid samples all of it at 1 s steps.

default.note: The binary mask and the emitted colour in one render. One sample per pixel with the box filter at its RNA minimum makes Cycles evaluate the same predicate a centre-sampling rasteriser does, because the integer raster coordinate is the pixel centre and the sample never leaves +/-0.005 px of it. A still costs one frame, so the full 1280x720 is affordable here where an animated case has to buy its grid.

seed-shift.note: The same recipe with the sampler's seed moved. At one sample per pixel of a deterministic emission there is nothing for a seed to change, so any pixel that moves between these two renders is the oracle's own noise rather than a disagreement with us -- which is what makes this the instrument floor instead of an assumption about it.

notes: A coverage case. Its shading -- textures, metallic-roughness, any extension it declares -- is NOT what this decides; board:1363 records why no case takes the shading arm yet. COLOR_0 is present in the file and is NOT what this decides: the material below declares the colour, so a vertex-colour disagreement cannot be read out of this case.

subjectFrameFraction.note: The fraction of the frame the subject's projected area covers at frame 0. RECOMPUTED BY THE RUNNER ON EVERY RUN and refused on mismatch, so what this line does is pin it. It is seeded from that recomputation, which makes it a DRIFT DETECTOR rather than a present-error check -- honest only because the camera is independently proven to be the framing rule's.
